claim_boundary: The Miller closure concerns quadratic characters of classical terminal Miller functions and finite products of them.
The support-to-cost separation is a counterexample to unrestricted degree or support based circuit lower bounds, not a parity evaluator.
Even-index division-polynomial characters over q=3 mod 4 remain open after the stated lower threshold.
No external point, wallet, real key or unknown production scalar is used.

covariance_classification.even_index_q_1_mod_4: psi_m changes sign but chi(-1)=+1, so the character remains invariant and is impossible
covariance_classification.even_index_q_3_mod_4: anti-invariant and symmetry-compatible; not solved by covariance alone
covariance_classification.odd_index: x-only and invariant under Q -> -Q, so impossible for canonical parity on every odd cycle
covariance_classification.uniform_mixed_mod4_transfer: a pure division-polynomial character cannot transfer unchanged across corpora containing both q=1 mod 4 and q=3 mod 4

division_polynomial.divisor_formula: div(psi_m)=sum_{T in E[m] minus {O}}[T]-(m^2-1)[O], for char(F_q) not dividing m

miller.interpretation: Miller-loop length does not create odd support because the line divisors telescope to at most two odd slots
miller.single_terminal_function_status: excluded by V8 whenever the required support lower bound exceeds two

review_status: the algebraic identities and executable checks are complete; literature source locking and formalization remain pending

support_to_cost_separation.decision: odd divisor support alone cannot imply square-root field-operation cost

surviving_secp256k1_frontier.status: open EDS-decimation problem; not an independent Miller route
